analysis.analysis_para1: European markets are broadly positive this morning, with the DAX up +0.65% and FTSE 100 gaining +0.08%, though the Nikkei 225 is slightly lower at -0.30%. Domestically, the falling 10-year yield at 4.44% provides a supportive backdrop for equities, particularly growth names. US market breadth remains healthy with 55.6% of stocks above their 50-day moving average (S5FI) and 61.8% above their 200-day (MMTH), indicating underlying strength despite mixed global performance.
analysis.analysis_para2: Given the positive pre-market momentum, particularly in tech, watch for the S&P 500 to establish support above the 7600 level early in the session. Confirmation of strength would involve the Nasdaq 100 sustaining its outperformance, signaling continued appetite for growth. Ideal entry points for leading stocks would be on a minor pullback to their 8-day exponential moving average or a test of prior breakout levels on declining volume. Maintain discipline with stop-loss orders as volatility, while normal, can pick up quickly.
